p: Watford sits on the north-west edge of London, close to the M25, and it's become a big draw for shopping, eating and nights out. The town centre is built around the Atria shopping centre and the High Street, with plenty of places to eat and drink. It's a handy spot for groups from across Hertfordshire and north-west London who want something fun without heading into the city.

Watford Junction station has fast trains to London Euston and the north, and the Overground and the Underground also reach Watford. If you're driving, the M1 and M25 are both close by, with car parks around the town centre.

For a group outing, book ahead and plan your teams. Mix the competitive players with the casual ones, and think about adding a few prizes to keep things interesting. It's also worth planning around Watford FC's home matches at Vicarage Road, as the town gets busy on matchdays.

If you've got a day to spare, the Warner Bros. Studio Tour London, where the Harry Potter films were made, is at Leavesden on the edge of Watford and draws fans from all over the world. You'll need to book it well in advance. The Watford Palace Theatre puts on a mix of shows throughout the year, and Whippendell Woods, next to Cassiobury Park, offers peaceful woodland walks.
